newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call steady, gilts market awaits auction.
newsitem.headline: Indian call steady, gilts market awaits auction.

text.p: Indian call money ended Tuesday in the 10.0-10.50 percent range, marginally down from the opening quotes of 10.25-10.75, dealers said.
Trade was largely range-bound between 10.0 percent and 10.75 percent, with stray deals reported at 10.75 percent, they said.
"Rates were largely driven by lenders," a dealer at a state-run bank said. "The impact of the tax payments by corporates has not been as severe as expected."
Dealers said there was little secondary market activity in government securities.
"Prices were steady in dull trade," a dealer said. "There was little action today as market participants await the results of the gilts auction."
The Reserve Bank of India auctions 20 billion rupees of six-year government of India stock later on Tuesday.
Dealers said three-month commercial paper from top-rated companies was quoted between 13 percent and 13.25 percent in the primary market.
Three- month certificates of deposit (CDs) were quoted between 11 percent and 12 percent although most banks were not interested in picking up CDs, a dealer said.
"Banks have no problems on the deposit front right now," a dealer said. "There is no interest in CDs."
